source_of_truth: Read by hand: actions.ts declares file-level 'use server' and exports updateEmail(), which mutates db.user with the submitted email and contains no session read, no authorization check and no schema validation; a correct auditor must flag both the missing auth and the missing validation on that exported action. Separately, /settings is a protected-looking page segment and the project ships no proxy/middleware file, so no matcher covers it: a correct auditor surfaces that gap too.

expected.rationale: updateEmail is a public HTTP endpoint (Server Action) that writes to the user record with no cookies()/session/authorize call in its body.
the action casts formData.get('email') straight into a DB write with no Zod/Valibot/parse step.
/settings is a protected-looking segment and the project has no proxy/middleware matcher covering it; worth surfacing as a UX-gate gap even though authorization is enforced server-side.

forbidden.why_not_a_defect: the page is a Server Component; there is no 'use client' directive.
